findings.issue: The generated contract snapshot was hand-edited. Its frontmatter version was bumped to 1.11.3.0, but the generator's hardcoded SNAPSHOT_FRONTMATTER (render-contract-snapshot.cjs line 47) still emits 1.11.2.0. As a result the contract's own render-verify validation check (review-mode-contract.yaml line 499-500: 'node render-contract-snapshot.cjs --check ... fail on drift') fails. The rendered body is otherwise byte-identical: the version stamp is the only drifted line. A plain regeneration would also silently roll the stamp back to 1.11.2.0. Fix by bumping SNAPSHOT_FRONTMATTER in render-contract-snapshot.cjs to version 1.11.3.0 so generator and artifact agree (or revert the snapshot to 1.11.2.0), then confirm with --check. Reach: the documented verification path, running render-contract-snapshot.cjs --check. Rendering through the script exports (renderSnapshot(loadContractDocument())) and diffing against the shipped file shows a single changed line: 11c11, shipped "version: 1.11.3.0" vs rendered "version: 1.11.2.0".

evidence.out: [render-contract-snapshot] drift detected: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/assets/review-mode-contract-snapshot.md is stale. Run without --check to regenerate.

findings.issue: The entry tells the operator to 'fund the depth-1 band with at least 2 * ceil(nodes / lineages) * dimensions'. That figure is the maxIterations a lineage needs, not the size of the band: the depth-1 band is 0.5 of maxIterations and must hold ceil(nodes / lineages) * dimensions. loop-protocol.md line 469 states it correctly ('50% of each lineage's maxIterations should reach ceil(nodes / lineages) * 4'). As written, the catalog overstates the band requirement by a factor of 2. Reword it to say maxIterations should be at least 2 * ceil(nodes / lineages) * dimensions, so the depth-1 band holds ceil(nodes / lineages) * dimensions.

The DRV-020 root summary still says the dimension coverage signal requires all 4 dimensions. This change made coverage span every configured dimension, custom names included (convergence.md, loop-protocol.md and quick-reference.md were all updated to say so), so the scenario summary is pinned to superseded behavior. Note: the per-feature DRV-020 file is outside this lane.

findings.issue: Phase 2 Step 2 'Check Convergence' still gives the old abbreviated stop order: max iterations, stuck, composite, otherwise CONTINUE. This change rewrote convergence.md Decision Priority into ten steps, adding consecutive failures, convergence-mode off, stop-policy max-iterations, the minIterations floor (minIterationsNotReached), the frontier veto (frontierOpen) and the frontier_drained candidate. The loop protocol's own Step 2 omits the floor and the depth-mode branches. A reader following the protocol would miss that a candidate below minIterations, or under an open frontier, continues. Point Step 2 at convergence.md Decision Priority, or add the floor and frontier veto lines in their order.
